```{r}
# 3. Función para limpiar tipos y columnas

delete_vars <- function(df, vars_to_remove) {
  # Convertir labelled a numeric para evitar errores
  df <- df %>% 
    mutate(across(everything(), ~ {
      if (inherits(., "labelled")) as.numeric(.) else .
    }))
  
  df <- df %>% select(-any_of(vars_to_remove))
  
  return(df)
}
```



```{r}
# Eliminar variables
vars_to_remove <- c(
  "urine", "dnrday", "prg2m", "prg6m", "surv2m", "surv6m", 
  "totmcst", "totcst", "income", "sfdm2", "adlp", 
  "death", "d.time", "dzclass", "adlsc", "sps", "avtisst", "glucose", "bun"
)

train_bio <- delete_vars(train_bio, vars_to_remove)
valid_bio <- delete_vars(valid_bio, vars_to_remove)
```

```{r}
# 5. Imputación: Calcular en TRAIN, aplicar a AMBOS
imputation_medians <- train_bio %>%
  group_by(dzgroup) %>%
  summarise(
    ## bun_med = median(bun, na.rm = TRUE),
    wblc_med = median(wblc, na.rm = TRUE),
    bili_med = median(bili, na.rm = TRUE),
    alb_med = median(alb, na.rm = TRUE),
    ph_med = median(ph, na.rm = TRUE),
    pafi_med = median(pafi, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

imputation_medians
```
```{r}
# Función para aplicar la imputación a cualquier set
apply_imputation <- function(df, medians) {
  df %>%
    left_join(medians, by = "dzgroup") %>%
    mutate(
      ## bun = ifelse(is.na(bun), bun_med, bun),
      wblc = ifelse(is.na(wblc), wblc_med, wblc),
      bili = ifelse(is.na(bili), bili_med, bili),
      alb = ifelse(is.na(alb), alb_med, alb),
      ph = ifelse(is.na(ph), ph_med, ph),
      pafi = ifelse(is.na(pafi), pafi_med, pafi)
    ) %>%
    select(-ends_with("_med"))
}

# Aplicar a ambos datasets
train_bio <- apply_imputation(train_bio, imputation_medians)
valid_bio <- apply_imputation(valid_bio, imputation_medians)
test_bio  <- apply_imputation(test_bio, imputation_medians)

# Aplicar la misma lógica de transformación que en tus gráficos
transform_edu <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    mutate(
      # Aseguramos que sea numérico primero por si acaso
      edu_num = as.numeric(as.character(edu)),
      edu_cat = case_when(
        edu_num <= 8  ~ "Basica",
        edu_num <= 12 ~ "Secundaria",
        edu_num > 12  ~ "Superior",
        TRUE          ~ "Unknown"
      ),
      # Convertimos a factor y definimos el orden lógico
      edu = factor(edu_cat, levels = c("Basica", "Secundaria", "Superior", "Unknown"))
    ) %>%
    select(-edu_num, -edu_cat) # Limpiamos columnas temporales
}

# Aplicar a tus datasets ya limpios
train_bio <- transform_edu(train_bio)
valid_bio  <- transform_edu(valid_bio)
test_bio  <- transform_edu(test_bio)

# Convertir categóricas a caracteres, asignar "Unknown" y luego a factor
cat_vars <- c("race", "dnr")
train_bio <- train_bio %>% mutate(across(all_of(cat_vars), ~replace_na(as.character(.), "Unknown")))
valid_bio <- valid_bio %>% mutate(across(all_of(cat_vars), ~replace_na(as.character(.), "Unknown")))
test_bio  <- test_bio %>% mutate(across(all_of(cat_vars), ~replace_na(as.character(.), "Unknown")))

# Imputar adls (8 como categoría)
train_bio <- train_bio %>% mutate(adls = replace_na(adls, 8))
valid_bio <- valid_bio %>% mutate(adls = replace_na(adls, 8))
test_bio  <- test_bio %>% mutate(adls = replace_na(adls, 8))

colSums(is.na(train_bio))
colSums(is.na(test_bio))
```

```{r}
# 1. Asegurar el target
train_bio$hospdead <- factor(train_bio$hospdead, 
                                 levels = c(0, 1), 
                                 labels = c("No", "Yes"))
valid_bio$hospdead <- factor(valid_bio$hospdead,
                                 levels = c(0, 1),
                                 labels = c("No", "Yes"))
test_bio$hospdead  <- factor(test_bio$hospdead, 
                                 levels = c(0, 1), 
                                 labels = c("No", "Yes"))

# 2. Convertir binarias categóricas que quedaron como 'num'
cols_to_factor <- c("diabetes", "dementia", "race", "dnr")

for(col in cols_to_factor) {
  train_bio[[col]] <- as.factor(train_bio[[col]])
  valid_bio[[col]] <- factor(valid_bio[[col]], levels = levels(train_bio[[col]]))
  test_bio[[col]]  <- factor(test_bio[[col]], levels = levels(train_bio[[col]]))
}


# Verificación final
str(train_bio)
```

```{r}
# 2. Creamos los datasets escalados
train_bio_scaled <- train_bio
valid_bio_scaled <- valid_bio
test_bio_scaled  <- test_bio

# Identificar columnas numéricas (excluyendo factores)
num_cols <- names(train_bio)[sapply(train_bio, is.numeric)]

# Aplicar escalado usando las estadísticas del train para ambos
for (col in num_cols) {
  mu <- mean(train_bio[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
  sigma <- sd(train_bio[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Aplicamos la fórmula: (valor - media) / desviación_estándar
  train_bio_scaled[[col]] <- (train_bio[[col]] - mu) / sigma
  valid_bio_scaled[[col]]  <- (valid_bio[[col]] - mu) / sigma
  test_bio_scaled[[col]]  <- (test_bio_scaled[[col]] - mu) / sigma
}

head(train_bio_scaled)
head(test_bio_scaled)
head(valid_bio_scaled)
```
